steps.title: Plane of movement
steps.body: An imaginary flat surface that divides the body into sections. Movement occurs ALONG or PARALLEL to a plane.

steps.title: Axis of movement
steps.body: An imaginary line around which the body or body part rotates. The axis is always PERPENDICULAR (at 90°) to the plane of movement.

steps.title: Sagittal Plane
steps.body: Divides the body into left and right halves. Movement in this plane involves flexion and extension - forward and backward movements.

steps.title: Transverse Axis
steps.body: Runs from left to right through the body. The body or body parts rotate around this axis when performing flexion and extension movements.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Name the three planes of movement and describe how each divides the body. | Which plane and axis are used when performing a forward somersault? | Explain why a cartwheel occurs in the frontal plane around the sagittal axis.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Sagittal plane - divides the body into left and right halves. Frontal plane - divides the body into front and back halves. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Plane and axis always come as a pair - learn them together Sagittal = left/right split; Frontal = front/back split; Transverse = top/bottom split The axis is always at 90° to its plane Use the exact terminology: "sagittal plane" not "side plane" Somersault = sagittal/transverse; Cartwheel = frontal/sagittal; Twist = transverse/longitudinal Common exam question: identify the plane and axis for a given sporting action Remember: most everyday movements (walking, running, sitting) occur in the sagittal plane
